description: Shared Renovate preset for all jdwlabs repositories — consumed as github>jdwlabs/.github.
Renovate is the single owner of dependency automation in this org; repository-level (UI) Dependabot should remain disabled so updates arrive through one reviewable pipeline.
Regular updates are batched weekly (non-major updates grouped into one PR per repo) to keep review load low; security/vulnerability fixes bypass the schedule and open immediately.

The weekly window is all of Saturday, UTC. Renovate only acts when a run happens to fall inside the window, and the hosted app does not run every repository at the same hour: a repository whose runs landed after a morning-only window went weeks with every update parked as awaiting schedule.

Lock files for JavaScript package managers are re-resolved in that same weekly window. A vulnerability fix only opens a PR for a dependency a manifest names, so a patched transitive package that its parent's range already accepts would otherwise stay stale until someone regenerated the lock file by hand.
Branches are kept rebased on the base branch so PRs stay fast-forward-clean for rebase-only merging.

packageRules.description: Batch all non-major updates into a single weekly PR per repo to keep noise reviewable

GitHub Actions updates are committed as ci(deps), not chore(deps). The release tooling on these repositories cuts a patch for chore(deps) so dependency fixes reach production, but an Action bump changes only CI: as chore(deps) it would publish an image, recreate a pod or redeploy a site with nothing in it that changed.
Non-major Action updates get a weekly group of their own. A group produces one commit, so mixing them with application dependencies would force a single commit type on both.

Lock file maintenance is limited to the npm manager, which also covers pnpm and Yarn. Re-resolving a Chart.lock or a Terraform provider lock changes what a GitOps repository deploys, and that should arrive as a named version bump someone chose, not as a side effect of a weekly refresh.

pnpm refuses to install a package published in the last 24 hours, so an update proposed sooner fails its own install step and never merges. Waiting a day here keeps Renovate from opening a pull request that cannot pass. Limited to the npm registry because the rule holds back any update whose source reports no publish time, which would stall chart and image updates indefinitely. Vulnerability fixes are exempt by Renovate's design and still open immediately.

customManagers.description: Release tooling run as `npx -p <package>@<version>` inside workflows, which no built-in manager reads. Without this the pins would never move.
